posts.name: Chrono
posts.cooked:
I had always assumed that these two characters were designed with cooperative play in mind, which you may miss out on a little in a solo electronic game. Chrono Ranger combos very well with damage boosters like Legacy and Ra and tends to take charge of attack plans with his bounty cards. He goes through cards fast, but he can also get help from other players on that.

Omnitron X works well with people that need cards to get going, such as Unity and Nightmist, and has plenty of cards to overcome frustrating hinderances like villain ongoing cards, horrible environment cards, and damage reduction.

I am sure that playstyle has a lot to do with it, but some of it may also be the solo play. These two heroes are build to want to work with other heroes (Chrono ranger in the lead, and Omnitron-X in support). Sort of an ENTJ/INFP combo if you are into Myers Briggs.

posts.cooked: Agree they do help promote interaction between the heroes, Chrono. Just Doin' My Job is one of my favorite examples of making the team work together in interesting ways. I don't know that it was a conscious decision, though.

posts.name: Ironic
posts.cooked:
I more see that as just GTG's evolving design sensibilities - Guise, Setback, and the Scholar all also interact a bunch with your teammates in ways the early characters seldom did, and later characters in general have a lot more tanking-style effects and damage boosts than in the base game + Rook City, where it was basically just Legacy for either of those niches.

 

Sell someone on the ST heroes?  Well, I think Ranger's a lot of fun, but if he's not your cuppa, there's a zillion other moderate buildup damage characters - Ra, Bunker, ExPat, Fixer, The Sentinels, K.Y.F.E... there's probably someone with a similar mechanical role to fit your playstyle, so I wouldn't get too hung up on any given one of them.  Omni-X, however, is much rarer - a really versatile support character in the vein of The Argent Adept and roughly nobody else - a lot more resilient agaist stuff destruction than the Adept.  As you say, he's busy at the start of a turn instead of the end, but that business can amount to whole extra turns with the Electro-Deployment Unity, so maybe think of that as the "turn," and the entire Play/Power/Draw as being the "end of turn" business?

Have to disagree with you on CR -- with the Masada, he's great against DR (even before getting Hunter and Hunted out, it can rival or surpass the kind of irreducible damage that Mr. Fixer can do unaided), The Ultimate Target means against some villains he is doing damage constantly (or at least until the dart thrower nerfs the villain's damage down to nothing -- and keep in mind that, like Stun Bolt, the dart thrower's DR applies even if no damage was done) and while he is vulnerable to Equipment destruction, I almost prefer to have his Bounties trashed, since he has a lot of ways to get them back into play or in hand. And he's one of the characters who can keep out his big boost with relatively little risk, since it doesn't come with self-damage like Pushing the Limits or Solar Flare. I've had him win games nearly single-handedly just for having Hunter and Hunted out for more than one turn.

posts.name: Agent Bon
posts.cooked:
Don't underestimate Chrono's other weapons, and don't overvalue the hat either.  If you're fighting an enemy with damage reduction, such as Apostate, The Masadah can do a lot for you.  Neuro-Toxin Dart Thrower is good for enemies where you get a lot of milage from reducting their damage output, such as Iron Legacy or Spite.  If you don't have a lot of spare cards then the hat just isn't essential, and I never use Displaced Amory to get it.

OX can be played not only as a character that builds up, but also as support.  If you're fighting an enemy that is likely to blow up his gear, you probably want to play him more in the support style.  Some heroes also benefit a lot from his support style.  His inherent power lets you play cards, or throw away cards, from any deck.  You can have Tempest put a card in play back on the opponent's deck, then have OX discard it, for example.  Unity benefits a lot from the extra plays since you don't have to lose cards to get the golems in play.  You can make other heroes that require setup get a jump-start the first few turns.  It is a very versatile power.

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked:
To be fair, most heroes have situations in which they have difficulty or keep losing their stuff or generally are pretty rubbish. Sometimes it's not even down to the villain or environment - Unity when she's got only equipment or only bots tends to just kind of sit around not doing very much, probably taking a turn or two to just draw two cards until she can actually get stuff out and do something useful. But if she does get set up, she wrecks stuff.

With Jim, his thing is focusing down a single, high hp target and pounding away at it with his self-buffed plinky damage that he can usually get set up for fairly quickly with his search cards if he doesn't manage to just draw them naturally anyway (and can also get a fair bit of extra draw too). His other equipment has uses, such as the Grenades for taking down annoying environment cards, or the Dart-Thrower to nerf damage or something. It's just that the main thing he does is totally demolish anything he decides to start focusing his fire on. He probably does more than Ra, I think, since Ra doesn't really do much except burn stuff in a variety of different ways and occasionally provide protection from Fire damage if people suddenly need it. Jim at least has a bunch of different weapons with side-effects that can provide some vague element of non-damaging stuff ;).

Omni-10 I see as a versatile support character who can also deal moderate damage and can actually be a pretty decent tank if there's only one damage type coming out (or if there are multiple types, if they're all of types that can be covered by the same plating ;)) if it's not in high enough quantities to do more than five damage to him a turn and break his components ;). And then he can heal people back up anyway, with the Innervation Rays :).

posts.name: Trajector
posts.cooked:
I think Chrono-Ranger is all about pulling the right bounty for the job at hand. The Ultimate Target can really shut down villains who do damage on hero turns - Matriarch, Spite, etc. The Whole Gang is terrific for penetrating damage reductions (certain Apostate relics come to mind). No Executions disrupts villains who rely on their trash (say, the Chairman or Citizen Hammer). You can always go for damage buffs and the Compounded Bow to pour out hits, but he really contributes to the team when a bounty does exactly what all the players need.

I’m not sure if his Best if Times promo is available in the app, but that really makes his bounties more interesting. I tend to focus bounties on the main villain, but with the Best of Times variant, I spread them around more - so I can use my power to focus them all on a single target, as well.

There are some universal mechanics inherent in deck based games that are always very strong, and straight up deck searches or "tutors" are one of them. Resource Ramping (like what Black Lotus and the Mox gems do), Cycling (which generally refers to an increased rate of card draw), and Milling (decreasing the opponents deck count and options/outs popularized by the card MillStone) are some of the others.

posts.name: Arcanist Lupus

My favorite combo will always be the zero-turn win in Lorwyn/Time Spiral standard.  Yes, there was a zero turn win made using only recent (well, recent at the time) cards.  Of course, it required that pretty much your entire starting hand be exactly what you need, so the probability of pulling it off was something around 0.0000002%, and the deck that would be needed would be pretty terrible otherwise (which is why it never saw play), but it was possible!

 

(For MtG players who want to know how the combo worked:  remove 4 Simian Spirit Guides from you hand for 4 mana.  Manamorphose two of that mana to blue, then play a [http://gatherer.wizards.com/Pages/Card/Details.aspx?multiverseid=130638]Pact[/url], but counter that Pact with Spellshift.  Spellshift reveals cards from the top of your library.  The next instant or sorcery is Dragonstorm, which then allows you to search for four Bogardian Hellkites, which enter play and deal 5 damage each to your opponent.  Boom.)
